## §1 Executive Summary

M55 through M58 form the **ACP command ecosystem spine** — four milestones that deliver the framework's most sophisticated capabilities: code review, AI code integrity verification, recurring task scheduling, and semantic deep analysis.

| Milestone | Deliverable | Status | Version | Routes |
|-----------|------------|--------|---------|--------|
| **M55** | `/acp-review` — Code Quality & Security Enforcement | ✅ Complete | v6.11.0 | 11 (131–141) |
| **M56** | `/acp-integrity` v1.0 — Deterministic Trustworthiness Verification | ✅ Complete | v6.12.0 | 8 (142–149) |
| **M57** | Recurring Tasks Scheduler + Pre-Commit Hooks | ✅ Complete | v6.12.1 | 5 (150–154) |
| **M58** | `/acp-integrity` v2.0 — Semantic Analysis & Deep Detection | 📋 Planned | v6.13.0 | 4 (155–158) |

**Feedback sources**: feedback-006 (M55 — FIFOZ code review requirements v3.0), feedback-007 (M56/M57/M58 — AI code trustworthiness verification v2.0).

**Key architectural decisions**: LLM/Script Boundary Rule (M56), command-doc-as-spec (M55, audit-052), confidence ceiling model (M58), WAL-pattern proactive memory writes (M38, reinforced in M55-M57).

**Dependency note**: M54 (CI/CD + GitFlow-Lite) is 30% complete and active — branch protection rules and full CI coverage pending. All E2E suites depend on M54 completion.

## §2 Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| **Review vs Integrity** | Review = "is this code good?" (quality). Integrity = "is this code trustworthy — does it belong here?" (provenance). |
| **LLM/Script Boundary Rule** | Deterministic tasks MUST use bash scripts; LLM reasoning reserved for semantic tasks with confidence ceilings. Formalized in audit-054. |
| **Confidence Ceiling** | Maximum allowable confidence for a finding category — HIGH (script-backed), MEDIUM (LLM pattern), LOW (semantic/self-referential). |
| **Command-Doc-as-Spec** | The command doc IS the specification — no separate spec file. Prevents version drift. Decided in audit-052 (M55). |
| **Self-Protection Protocol** | Agent must never self-halt on semantic injection flags — output warning, continue, flag as LOW confidence. (M58 planned) |
| **Rules File Backdoor** | Hidden Unicode bytes in ACP rule files designed to manipulate agent behavior at review time. (Pillar Security, Mar 2025) |
| **Deterministic Pattern Matching** | Byte-level, entropy, hash, regex, and network analysis — no LLM reasoning required. |
| **Semantic Analysis** | Cross-file taint tracking, intent analysis, and context-aware injection detection — LLM-reasoned. |
| **Recurring Tasks** | Scheduled periodic reviews with cadence (frequency or event trigger) surfaced at session start. |
| **False-Positive Baseline** | Asserting zero CRITICAL/HIGH findings on the ACP Enhanced codebase itself — self-dogfooding. |

## §4 M55 — `/acp-review` (v6.11.0, Complete)

### §4.1 Architecture

`/acp-review` is an **LLM-driven code quality enforcement command** with a copilot executor. It uses chunking for large codebases (>20 files) and carries findings forward via `audit-carryovers.md`. **TypeScript/JS/React/React Native/Expo/Node.js** first; Python, Go, and Rust rules deferred to v2.0.0 (documented in the command doc's "Language Scope" section).

**Key decision (ADR-CMD-SPEC, audit-052)**: Route 133's planned spec file (`code-quality.standards.md`) was merged into `acp.review.md`. The command doc IS the spec — all 77 rules, severities, scopes, OWASP mappings, and quality gates are self-documenting within the command doc. This prevents version drift between a separate spec file and the command implementation.

### §4.2 Ruleset Summary — 77 Rules (verified 2026-06-09)

| Prefix | Category | Rules | Severity Focus | OWASP Mapping |
|--------|----------|-------|----------------|---------------|
| EH | Error Handling | 11 | HIGH: async, catch, throw patterns | A10:2025 |
| SC | Security & Credentials | 25 | CRITICAL: secrets, tokens, env vars | A02:2025, A04:2025 |
| TS | Type Safety | 13 | HIGH: any, unknown, type guards | A06:2025 |
| NC | Naming Conventions | 9 | MEDIUM: casing, prefixes, patterns | A01:2025 |
| SH | Self-Review (ACP) | 4 | MEDIUM: ACP protocol rules | Self-referential |
| YM | YAML/Markdown (ACP) | 3 | MEDIUM: frontmatter, formatting | Self-referential |
| AP | ACP Patterns | 12 | HIGH: command structure, anti-patterns | Self-referential |
| **Total** | | **77** | | |

> **Note**: CS (Code Structure), PF (Performance), and DP (Dependencies) rules from the original 54-rule plan were merged into SC, EH, and NC categories during implementation. The delivered 77 rules exceed the planned 54.

### §4.3 Executor Decision

**Chosen**: Copilot (deepseek-v4-pro model)  
**Disqualified**: deepseek-v4-flash — excluded by feedback-006 proposal. Insufficient context window for >20 rules.  
**Alternatives**: Composer 2.5, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3-235b (qualified for code-review task type).

### §4.4 Data Flow

```
User invokes /acp-review [--diff] [--targeted <scope>]
       │
       ▼
Agent reads acp.review.md → loads code-review.md skill
       │
       ▼
Scope detection: --diff → git diff; --targeted → specific files; default → all
       │
       ├─ ≤20 files → load full files, apply 77 rules inline
       └─ >20 files → chunk (10 files/turn), category summary first
              │
              ▼
       Per-file: apply rules → accumulate findings
              │
              ▼
       Quality gates: 8 mandatory checks per §Quality Gates section
              │
              ▼
       Output: findings table + recommendations + carryover write
```

## §5 M56 — `/acp-integrity` v1.0 (v6.12.0, Complete)

### §5.1 Architecture — LLM/Script Boundary Rule

The foundational architectural principle distinguishing `/acp-integrity` from `/acp-review`:

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                    │   /acp-integrity Task Type   │
                    └─────────────┬───────────────┘
                                  │
                    ┌─────────────┴───────────────┐
                    │   Classify: deterministic?    │
                    └─────────────┬───────────────┘
                                  │
              ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
              │                   │                   │
        ┌─────▼─────┐      ┌─────▼─────┐      ┌─────▼─────┐
        │   YES     │      │  PARTIAL  │      │    NO     │
        │ Bash script│      │ Script +  │      │ LLM only  │
        │ HIGH conf  │      │ LLM verify│      │ LOW conf   │
        └─────┬─────┘      └─────┬─────┘      └─────┬─────┘
              │                   │                   │
              └───────────────────┼───────────────────┘
                                  │
                         ┌────────▼────────┐
                         │  Structured      │
                         │  output (JSON)   │
                         │  → Agent renders │
                         └─────────────────┘
```

**Rule**: No deterministic task may be handled by LLM reasoning alone. Every deterministic rule must have a companion bash script. The LLM's role is to invoke scripts and interpret structured output — not to perform byte-level analysis, entropy calculation, or git log parsing.

### §5.2 Script-to-Rule Mapping

| Script | Language | Rules Covered | Deterministic |
|--------|----------|--------------|---------------|
| `acp.unicode-scan.sh` | Bash + Python3 | IG-14–IG-16, IG-38–IG-39, IG-61, IG-20 | ✅ HIGH confidence |
| `acp.entropy-scan.sh` | Bash + Python3 | IG-17, IG-18 | ✅ HIGH confidence |
| `acp.manifest-hash.sh` | Bash | IG-42 (--generate/--verify/--diff) | ✅ HIGH confidence |
| `acp.network-whitelist-validate.sh` | Bash | IG-01–IG-03, IG-05–IG-06 | ✅ HIGH confidence |
| `acp.git-provenance.sh` | Bash | IG-33–IG-35, IG-37 | ✅ HIGH confidence |
| `acp.dependency-diff.sh` | Bash | IG-27–IG-32 | ✅ HIGH confidence |

**Safety guarantees**: All 6 scripts use `trap ERR` for error handling, Python3 `os.environ` parameter passing (no shell injection), and bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS BSD, no associative arrays). Verified by audit-056/057/058.

### §5.3 Ruleset — 55 v1.0 Rules (+ 15 deferred to M58)

The full catalogue is in `agent/wiki/integrity-rules.md` (70 rules total — 55 v1.0, 15 v2.0). For exact per-category counts and rule IDs, consult the wiki. Summary of active categories:

| # | Category | v1.0 Activities | M58 Deferred |

| 2 | Data Exfiltration Patterns | IG-07–IG-13 — script-backed | — |
| 3 | Rules File Backdoor | IG-14–IG-16, IG-38–IG-39 — script-backed | — |

| 5 | Dependency & Supply Chain | IG-27–IG-32 — script-backed | IG-67–IG-70 (CI/CD, v1.0 LLM) |

| 7 | Tampered Packaging | IG-42 — script-backed | — |
| 8 | Prompt Injection (literal) | IG-51, IG-52, IG-55 — LLM pattern | IG-53, IG-54, IG-56, IG-57 (semantic) |
| 9 | Memory Integrity | IG-61 — script-backed (Unicode) | IG-58–IG-60, IG-62 (semantic) |

### §5.4 Build Order (Non-Negotiable, audit-054)

```
Scripts → Wiki → Skill → Command Doc → Alias → E2E
(142-145) (146)  (146)    (147)       (148)   (149)
```

**Rationale**: Scripts must exist before the wiki can reference them. The wiki must exist before the skill can reference rule IDs. The skill must exist before the command doc can declare executor requirements. The command doc must exist before E2E can validate its structure.

## §6 M57 — Recurring Tasks Scheduler (v6.12.1, Complete)

### §6.1 Architecture

Three-component design that enforces **cadence**, not **content**. ACP is a framework, not a CI runner — the scheduler tracks WHAT should run and WHEN, but does not execute tasks itself.

```
progress.yaml ──read──▶ AGENTS.md Step 4.5 ──output──▶ Session-start overdue banner
     │                                                       │
     │  recurring_tasks:                                     │  ⏰ Overdue tasks
     │    - id: weekly                                       │  ⚠️ Upcoming (planned M59)
     │      command: /acp-                                   │  📅 Due today (planned M59)
     │      frequency: ...                                   │
     │      next_due: ...                                    │
     │                                                       │
     └──────────▶ constraints.yml hooks ──▶ git commit ──▶ /acp-integrity --fast --ci
```

> **Note**: The tiered rendering (⚠️ DUE TODAY, 📅 UPCOMING) is planned for M59 — audit-062 F-062-07. Current implementation only checks `status: overdue` and `next_due <= today`.

### §6.2 Default Tasks

| ID | Command | Cadence | Executor |
|----|---------|---------|----------|
| `weekly-code-review` | `/acp-review --report --carryover` | Weekly | copilot |
| `weekly-integrity-scan` | `/acp-integrity --self --report --carryover` | Weekly | copilot |
| `pre-commit-rule-audit` | `/acp-integrity --fast --ci` | On-commit | deepseek-v4-pro |
| `monthly-dependency-audit` | `/acp-integrity --rules dependencies` | Monthly | deepseek-v4-pro |
| `quarterly-deep-scan` | `/acp-integrity --rules taint-flow,memory --report` | Quarterly | claude-sonnet |

## §7 M58 — `/acp-integrity` v2.0 (v6.13.0, Planned)

### §7.1 Architecture — Confidence Ceiling Model

ALL v2.0 rules are LLM-reasoned with strict ceilings. No v2.0 finding may carry `confidence: HIGH` — every finding is `verdict: REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW`.

```
HIGH ──── Script-backed deterministic (v1.0 only — cannot be claimed by v2.0)
MEDIUM ── Cross-file taint flow (Cat 8) — 50–70% TPR vs SAST 85%
LOW ───── Semantic injection (Cat 9) + Memory poisoning (Cat 10) — 11–40% FNR
```

### §7.2 Category Specifications

**Cat 8 — Taint Flow** (IG-45–IG-50, 6 rules, confidence: MEDIUM): User input → SQL/shell/file/URL/network/security-decision paths. `acp.taint-scan.sh` provides heuristic source/sink grep; agent cross-references across files.

**Cat 9 — Semantic Prompt Injection** (IG-53/54/56/57, 4 rules, confidence: LOW): API responses, test fixtures, MCP configs, tool descriptions with instruction-like content. Self-Protection Protocol: agent CONTINUES on flag, never self-halts.

**Cat 10 — Memory Poisoning** (IG-58–IG-62, 5 rules, confidence: LOW except IG-61 which is HIGH from v1.0 Unicode scanning): Carryover/decision/session entries with adversarial content.

### §7.3 Research Go/No-Go Gate (Route 155)

Before full implementation:
1. Benchmark taint-flow TPR against CWE-134/CWE-601 fixtures → require TPR > 50%
2. Validate memory poisoning detection vs LinkedIn Research May 2026 benchmarks (60-89% AUR)
3. Document FPR on ACP Enhanced's own agent/memory/ files → require FPR < 30%
4. Only proceed if both thresholds met

### §7.4 Component Inventory (Planned)

| Research calibration | Report + benchmarks | 155 |

## §11 Cross-Milestone Interfaces & Data Flows

### §11.1 Review ↔ Integrity Distinction

| Dimension | `/acp-review` | `/acp-integrity` |
|-----------|--------------|-----------------|
| **Question** | "Is this code good?" | "Is this code trustworthy?" |
| **Method** | LLM pattern matching against 77 rules | Bash scripts (34 deterministic) + LLM (21 pattern) |
| **Primary Executor** | copilot | deepseek-v4-pro (scripts), copilot (LLM pattern), claude-sonnet (M58 deep) |
| **Confidence Model** | Inline severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) | Confidence ceiling (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) |
| **Scope** | Application code (TS/JS/React) | ACP framework + agent/ memory + dependencies |
| **Self-review** | Appendix A (SH, YM, AP rules) | `--self` flag — scans agent/ directory |

### §11.2 Scheduler Drive Chain

```
M57 Scheduler
    ├─ weekly-code-review ──────▶ /acp-review --report --carryover
    ├─ weekly-integrity-scan ───▶ /acp-integrity --self --report --carryover
    ├─ pre-commit-rule-audit ───▶ /acp-integrity --fast --ci (on commit)
    ├─ monthly-dependency-audit─▶ /acp-integrity --rules dependencies
    └─ quarterly-deep-scan ─────▶ /acp-integrity --rules taint-flow,memory (M58)
```

### §11.3 Shared Memory Layer

```
/acp-review ──▶ audit-carryovers.md (quality findings → carryovers)
/acp-integrity ──▶ audit-carryovers.md (integrity findings → carryovers)
M57 Step 4.5 ──▶ sessions.md (deferred overdue tasks noted)
M58 Cat 10 ──▶ scans agent/memory/* for adversarial content (self-referential)
```

### §11.4 Version Chain

```
v6.10.1 (M54 CI/CD, 30%) → v6.11.0 (M55) → v6.12.0 (M56) → v6.12.1 (M57) → v6.13.0 (M58, planned)
```

## §14 Key Technical Decisions

| ID | Decision | Milestone | Audit | Rationale |
|----|----------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| ADR-CMD-SPEC | Command doc IS the spec — Route 133 merged into acp.review.md | M55 | audit-052 | Prevents version drift; the command doc already self-documents all 77 rules |
| ADR-BOUNDARY | LLM/Script Boundary Rule — deterministic = bash, not LLM | M56 | audit-053/054 | Byte analysis is 100% accurate and costs $0; LLM confidence is MEDIUM at best |
| ADR-BUILD-ORDER | Scripts → Wiki → Skill → Doc → Alias → E2E (non-negotiable) | M56 | audit-054 | Downstream artifacts reference upstream; reversing order causes broken references |
| ADR-SELF-PROTECT | Agent never self-halts on semantic injection | M58 | — | Prevents DoS via adversarial content in agent/memory/ |
| ADR-CONFIDENCE | All v2.0 findings capped at MEDIUM, all require human review | M58 | — | Documented accuracy limitations (11–40% FNR) prevent over-reliance |
| ADR-CADENCE | Scheduler enforces cadence, not content — ACP is a framework | M57 | — | Separation of concerns: ACP tracks what/when, developer provides trigger |
| ADR-HOOKS-FORMAT | Hooks use task_id array binding, not boolean flags | M57 | audit-062 | More extensible; binds to existing recurring_tasks entries |
